newsitem.title: USA: LSI Logic firms as PlayStation fears fade.
newsitem.headline: LSI Logic firms as PlayStation fears fade.

text.p: Shares of LSI Logic Corp firmed in brisk trade Thursday, as rumors the chip maker would lose its share of the Sony Corp PlayStation business to Toshiba Corp were put to rest by analysts.
LSI Logic, whose shares had dipped on concerns that Toshiba won the next Sony PlayStation design, recovered as analysts at Lehman Brothers and Robertson Stephens made positive comments on the stock.
The shares were up 1-3/4 at 31-1/8, on NYSE trading volume of 3.4 million shares.

Lehman Brother analyst Michael Gumport said LSI Logic already shared the PlayStation business with Toshiba. Toshiba's cut of that business might increase, but it would not eliminate LSI Logic, he said.

"LSI makes the logic chip and Toshiba contributes a companion graphic chip," Gumport said in a research note. "Our current understanding is that there is a potential for a more equal contribution from the key suppliers."

Robertson Stephens analyst Daniel Niles said LSI Logic was his top stock pick for the upcoming quarter, and he thought the shares would appreciate 70 percent to $50 per share over the next 12 months. This was based on a $2.00 per share earnings estimate for 1998, he said.
"There is a lot of misinformation around the company," he said. "There have been calls that LSI Logic would lose its share of the Sony PlayStation business, which is untrue."
Niles said he thought the company met consensus earnings estimates in the recent quarter, and that LSI Logic would continue to grow while expanding margins in the September quarter.
